RagShortTexts: The economic sustenance of Votadinians in 374 AD relied upon extensive agrarian estates, pastoral herds, and strategic mineral extraction.
Anchored around commercial hubs near Traprain Law Hillfort, merchant caravans traded valuable bullion, grain, wine, and exotic raw goods.
Advanced weapon smithies and metallurgical workshops provided the industrial backbone necessary to equip large armies in the field.

Variants.Content: Underpinning the immense martial demands of Votadinians was an agrarian and mercantile economic system rooted in rural estates and municipal workshops. Across fertile valleys and pastures, countless tenant farmers and laborers produced wheat harvests, vintage wines, cured pelts, and high-grade iron ingots destined for storehouses. Within thriving market plazas around Traprain Law Hillfort, cosmopolitan merchants converged to barter gold coinage, imported silks, fine armaments, and livestock. Imperial or royal customs officials maintained toll gates, extracting heavy excise duties from freight wagons. Yet the system faced constant vulnerability from harvest failures and trade route disruptions, compelling rulers to enforce grain requisitions to sustain armies in the field.

Our wagon train crawls up the glen road, and the drivers shout over the wind to keep the oxen moving. Grain is issued in hard biscuits that have to be soaked before a man can chew them. Wages come as bronze pennies and a few silver pieces, and each man counts his share twice before the next muster.

The reeve of the hill estates reads the tally board by peat fire: the smiths turned out one hundred and twenty horseshoes and fifty spearheads in the last quarter. Cured fish and wool sold at the coastal fair cover the mail of the household knights. Every bale of wool passing the hill toll is entered in the lord's ledger.
